Brief-0 (port CholeskyQR to n=1024 B=60) EXHAUSTED with a NEGATIVE result: CholeskyQR is not competitive at this shape. Best benchmark from the 3 cholqr iterations was 5975us geomean (worse than the 2081us baseline) because shape 4/8/11 went ~3778us->274000us. Branch reset to the byte-identical baseline (no change committed forward). Findings: (1) The orhr_col LU RECON dominates at B=60 -- ~22ms alone (latency-bound diag_lu over 16 serial 64-blocks, 1 CTA/matrix underfills) vs the FP16 panel's ~3.8ms TOTAL, so CholeskyQR can never beat the panel here regardless of Gram/TRSM speed. (2) shape4 cond=2 is a 100:1 COLUMN-SCALING -> cond(A)~4e4, so a 3xTF32 batched Gram gives a NON-PD G (cholesky fails); only an FP64 Gram (batched bmm ~3.8ms, faster than int-Ozaki's ~6.5ms per-matrix loop) stays PD. (3) The recon's TF32 Schur GEMMs amplify orth error ~6x; 1-pass gives 3.7e-2 (>0.0122 gate), CholeskyQR2 reorthogonalizes to ~9e-3 on the bench seed but the differential guard's other seeds hit 0.020-0.027 -- still failing, with seed variance. (4) Two real BUGS found in the matured n=4096 cholqr code that break at n!=4096: chol_L_to_R_out zeroes R's off-diagonals (only the diagonal transposes), and the int-Ozaki Gram per-matrix _int_mm loop serializes at B=60. SUGGESTED NEXT DIRECTION: do NOT pursue CholeskyQR for n=1024/2048; the FP16 two-level panel is far better there. Instead point briefs at the panel kernel itself (it's ~53% of shape-4 GPU time, latency-bound on its within-panel rank-1 sync chain) -- e.g. wider OB via dynamic-smem build_Minv, deeper inner-panel pipelining, or msplit (multi-CTA per matrix) to fill the 148 SMs at B=60.

Keep PAF (first inner block fused), m-split ONLY the standalone last-block panel (cm-OV, P=2). geomean 2174us (better than iter0 2260 but still +4.4% vs 2081 baseline). The cross-CTA barrier overhead OVERWHELMS the m/P row-pass shortening at b=32, m<=992. Multi-CTA m-split is NOT viable at this scale (matches the microbench: grid.sync ~1.4us; and matches why the champion deleted msplit). Pivoting to the intra-CTA cm_coop/HELP path (cheap __barrier_sync_count, no device fence) which cuts the SAME per-column critical path at the existing 60 CTAs.

CONCLUSION: multi-CTA m-split is conclusively NON-VIABLE for the n=1024 panel -- the cross-CTA group barrier (~33/panel, each with 2 device-scope __threadfence ~1.5us) costs ~50us/panel ALONE, approaching the entire single-CTA panel cost (63us), so no SM-fill can compensate. WHAT I DID: (1) Profiled shape-4 in ISOLATION (the brief's ask). Ground truth: the n=1024 panel is TWO one-CTA-per-matrix kernels - qr_panel_apply_fused_kernel (40.9%) + standalone panel_factor_smem_wsp_ov_bf16 (27%) = 68% of shape-4. ncu confirms the brief's premise: Grid=60, Waves/SM=0.41, 17.9% SM throughput, Block-Limit-SharedMem=1 -> 60/148 SMs, BARRIER-LATENCY-bound. (2) RESURRECTED the deleted panel_factor_smem_wsp_cm_ov_bf16_msplit_kernel (the genuine multi-CTA m-split, from champion 46cf107f - it uses a race-free global-atomic sense-reversing GROUP barrier + double-buffered partials + 1-barrier/column, NOT cudaLaunchCoop) and the g_msplit/g_msplit_minm knobs + launch + high-smem opt-in. Tested 3 configs at P=2: (a) full-smem + PAF-off + cm-OV path -> 2260us (shape4 +62%); (b) PAF kept, m-split only the standalone last-block panel -> 2174us; (c) PER-CTA-COMPACT-SMEM m-split (each CTA holds only b+ds rows, smem 131->66KB) -> 2174us. All validate PASS (the kernel is numerically bit-identical).

ROOT CAUSE (well-evidenced): the cross-CTA group barrier costs ~1.5us each (matches a standalone grid.sync microbench: 1.4us/sync on this B200) and the panel needs ~b+1=33/panel; that ~50us/panel of barrier+device-fence overhead ALONE approaches the entire single-CTA panel cost (63us avg), so the m/P row-pass shortening can never net-win. The compact-smem variant DID fill more SMs (ncu: 60->120 SMs, Waves 0.41->0.81) but register pressure (64 reg/thread) still caps 1 CTA/SM, so the barrier spin is NOT hidden by a co-resident group, and per-launch stayed 158us = 2.5x the single-CTA 64us. This is also why the prior champion deleted msplit (at n=512 B=640 the SMs are already full so it only added cost; at n=1024 B=60 the SM gap exists but the barrier cost is the killer regardless).

The brief's stated mechanism premise is also slightly off: the n=2048 _LARGE_HI 'wsp_help/cm_coop machinery' is MULTI-WARP within ONE CTA (intra-CTA __barrier_sync_count, no device fence), NOT multiple CTAs per matrix - both LO and HI are 1-CTA/matrix. So there was no multi-CTA machinery to 'adapt'; I built the real one and it loses.

SUGGESTED NEXT DIRECTIONS (for a fresh brief, NOT pursued here): (1) The cm_coop/HELP path (intra-CTA, cheap barrier) + float4 column-major m-passes are the codebase's PROVEN critical-path lever, but they require dropping PAF+ov_fold (mutually exclusive in the run_panel dispatch) which itself regressed in my config (a) - so a clean test needs an OV-FOLD variant of cm_coop OR a float4+HELP rewrite of the PAF kernel's panel phase. (2) FEWER barriers per panel: a multi-column-per-barrier panel (like the existing cm2 N-reflectors-per-barrier, currently used for n=176/352) ported to the LO panel would cut the 32-barrier chain to ~16/~11, directly reducing the latency-bound stall count at the existing 60 CTAs - this is single-CTA (no cross-CTA cost) and is the most promising un-tried direction. (3) The n=1024 LO path (single-CTA PAF megakernel + ov-fold) is a tightly-coupled, well-tuned local optimum; gains here are likely small. Consider whether shape-3 (n=512 B=640, the LARGEST GPU-time shape) has more headroom than n=1024.
